problem:
Find the radius and center of the circle whose equation is
$2{x}^{2}+2{y}^{2}-8x+8y+3=0.$

feedback.problem: Find the center and radius of the circle whose equation is ${x}^{2}+2x+2y+{y}^{2}+1=0.$
feedback.worked_solution:
To find the center and radius of the circle, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares.

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+2x+2y+{y}^{2}+1 & =0 \\ ({x}^{2}+2x)+({y}^{2}+2y) & =-1 \\ ({x}^{2}+2\cdot x+{1}^{2})+({y}^{2}+2\cdot y+{1}^{2}) & =-1+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2} \\ ({x}^{2}+2\cdot x+{1}^{2})+({y}^{2}+2\cdot y+{1}^{2}) & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can factor the perfect squares and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+1)^{2}+(y+1)^{2} & ={1}^{2} \\ (x-(-1))^{2}+(y-(-1))^{2} & ={1}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the circle is centered at $(-1,-1)$ and its radius is $1.$
